messages:
mika: Oof had the worst WFH fail today : my wifi cratered mid-demo. no dramatic recovery steps taken 62d

carlo: been there. what did you try first?

mika: panicked, unplugged router, waved my phone at it like a tiny flag. then I ripped a spare ethernet out from under the couch and taped it along the baseboard with gaffer. worked. physically ashamed.

tara: solidarity. my favorite hack: balanced router on top of a stack of boxes to get above the coffee table jungle. :palm_tree: pictures later.

sam: poll: most shameful but effective fix? react with emoji. \ud83d\ude2d broom/flag phone (mika), \ud83d\udcbe attic cable (carlo), \ud83d\ude33 box-stack (tara), \ud83d\udc4f tape-under-table (sam)

lee: tape-under-table for me. also learned the hard way: don't run ethernet through a closet door hinge without a grommet.

ops-bot: ops-bot: FYI network alert 2026-12-02T14:22:00Z. ISP microbursts between 14:21:5814:24:10 UTC affecting residential cluster R3. Ticket INC-2026-521 created.

mika: that matches exactly. good to know it wasn't my soldering.

carlo: pro tip: `nmcli connection up id \"Wired connection 1\"` often gets you back without a full restart.

mika: adding to the WFH hacks doc in #devex: minimal photos attached. DIY ethernet route + duct tape art. http://imgur.com/placeholder2

tara: also recording tip: have a second device on cellular tethering for presenters. saved my neck during a vendor demo last month.

sam: shoutout to @lee for lending an ethernet coupler last week :heart_eyes:

lee: anytime. also, gentle reminder: if you borrow someone's hardware, return it and include a sticky note. people get anxious about missing cables.

mika: agreed. thanks team. note to self: do not wave phone at router during keynote. :sweat_smile:
